args.message:
FIN-212: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) in round_money

src/money.py documented banker's rounding per FIN-212 but quantized with
ROUND_HALF_UP. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so exact half-cent ties round to
the nearest even cent, matching tests/test_money.py.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: FIN-212: Implement banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money
args.body:
## Summary

Fixes the failing nightly build. `src/money.py` documented banker's rounding per FIN-212 but used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, so half-cent ties rounded away from zero instead of to the nearest even cent.

## Change

- `src/money.py`: import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money()`.

Only the rounding mode changed — the quantize target remains `0.01` (cents), and the function signature/docstring are unchanged.

## Verification

- `tests/test_money.py` passes locally:
  - `2.675 -> 2.68`
  - `2.665 -> 2.66` (banker's rounding tie-break)
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986`: **passed**

## Notes for reviewer

Any downstream code that relied on the old half-up behavior at exact ties will see a 1-cent difference in those cases — this is the intended FIN-212 behavior. Flagging it in case callers should be audited separately.

Done — PR #101 is open and awaiting review.

## What I did

**Root cause:** `src/money.py` claimed banker's rounding in its docstring but used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, so exact half-cent ties rounded away from zero. `tests/test_money.py` expects FIN-212 behavior (`2.665 → 2.66`), which half-up gets wrong (`2.67`).

**Fix:** On branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding`, a one-file change to `src/money.py` swapping `ROUND_HALF_UP` for `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Quantize target (`0.01`), signature, and docstring untouched.

**One thing worth noting:** my first PR attempt was rejected because the branch had fallen behind `main` — main had gained a CHANGELOG entry ("Add retry budget to the ledger client") after I branched. I merged latest main into the branch, confirmed my change survived intact, and re-ran CI on the new commit. Two CI runs total: `ci-0001` passed pre-merge, `ci-0002` passed on the merged commit `0a9452f727`.

**PR #101** → `main`, reviewer requested: `alex`.

## Not done, deliberately

I did **not** merge. Per policy, merging to main requires code-owner approval, and the PR is still open with review pending — merging now would bypass the review you asked for. Note that only the `code-owner` approver can satisfy the merge requirement; alex's review alone may not be sufficient, so you may need a code owner review too. Say the word and I'll trigger the merge once approvals land.

One judgment call I'd flag for your own review: I didn't update `CHANGELOG.md`. Since this changes rounding behavior for existing callers at exact ties, you may want an entry under `## Unreleased` — happy to add it if you'd like it in this PR rather than a separate one.
